tax_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me calculate our Delaware franchise tax liability before we file the annual report. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for any inputs you need if I haven't provided them: our Delaware entity name and file number, total authorized shares (from our certificate of incorporation or any amendments), total issued shares outstanding, and our total gross assets (from our most recent balance sheet, as required for the Assumed Par Value Capital Method).

2. Using the Delaware Division of Corporations' published franchise tax rules, calculate the tax under BOTH methods available to corporations:
 - Authorized Shares Method (based solely on the number of authorized shares, using their current tiered rate table)
 - Assumed Par Value Capital Method (based on authorized shares, issued shares, and total gross assets, using their current formula and rate)

3. Show your full calculation work for each method step by step so I can verify the numbers.

4. Identify which method produces the lower tax amount, since Delaware allows us to pay the lesser of the two.

5. Note the applicable annual report filing fee for our entity type, and add it to get the total amount due.

6. Flag anything unusual (e.g., if our gross assets or share counts seem to trigger the maximum tax cap, or if authorized shares changed mid-year).

When done, report back: the calculated tax under both methods, which one is lower, the annual report fee, the total amount due, and a summary of the inputs and formulas used so I can double-check accuracy. Do not submit any filing or payment — this calculation is preparation only for the next filing step.

tax_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for our Delaware franchise tax and annual report filing by gathering the officer and director information Delaware requires. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for our company's exact legal name and Delaware business entity file number if you don't already have them (needed to look up or confirm the filing on the Delaware Division of Corporations site).
2. Ask me to confirm the current officer roster (at minimum, one officer such as President, Secretary, or Treasurer) and the full board of directors as of today, including full legal names and titles for each person.
3. Ask me for a current mailing address for each officer and director, since Delaware's annual report requires this.
4. Check any existing internal records I can share (cap table notes, prior year's filing, board resolutions, or corporate bylaws) for names/titles/addresses that may need updating, and flag any discrepancies you find between those records and what I confirm verbally or in writing.
5. Compile all gathered officer and director data into a clean, organized summary (a simple table with columns: Name, Title, Address) formatted so it can be directly transcribed into the Delaware annual report filing form.
6. Note any missing or unclear information as open items and list them explicitly so I can fill the gaps.

Do not attempt to submit anything to the Delaware Division of Corporations or any other filing system — this step is only about collecting and organizing the required officer and director data. Do not access or request any passwords, API keys, or other credentials; if you need to log into a portal to check prior filings, use your configured credentials.

When done, report back with: the completed officer/director table, a list of any open questions or missing details, and confirmation that the data is ready to be handed off for the actual franchise tax and annual report filing step.

tax_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare (but NOT submit) our company's annual Delaware franchise tax and annual report filing on the Delaware Division of Corporations ICIS portal (https://icis.corp.delaware.gov/ecorp/logintax.aspx).

First, ask me for anything you need that's missing, including: our Delaware business entity name and file number, the total number of authorized shares, par value per share, total gross assets and total issued shares as of fiscal year-end (needed for the Assumed Par Value Capital Method calculation, if applicable), the name and title of the officer who will sign, the registered agent's information, and our configured portal login credentials access.

Then do the following:
1. Using your configured credentials, log into the ICIS portal.
2. Navigate to the annual franchise tax and annual report filing flow for our entity.
3. Fill in all required fields: entity details, share structure, officer/director information, and registered agent details.
4. Use the portal's built-in calculator (or standard Delaware franchise tax formulas) to compute the estimated franchise tax due under both the Authorized Shares Method and the Assumed Par Value Capital Method, and note which yields the lower tax.
5. Prepare a summary showing: entity name/file number, all figures entered, calculated tax due, and the officer name/title who must attest and sign.
6. Do NOT click submit, attest, or pay on my behalf — this filing requires an officer's legal attestation under Delaware law and must stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the completed draft filing summary, the calculated franchise tax amount(s), any missing or ambiguous data you need me to confirm, and confirmation that the filing is staged in the portal but not submitted, awaiting my review and attestation.

tax_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the annual Delaware franchise tax filing and payment on the Delaware Division of Corporations site (https://corp.delaware.gov/paytaxes/). Please do all the preparatory work, then stop before authorizing any payment.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our exact company name as registered in Delaware, our Delaware file number, the tax year being filed, our total gross assets and total issued shares (needed for the Assumed Par Value Capital Method calculation, if applicable), and our authorized shares count. Also ask whether we want to use the Authorized Shares Method or Assumed Par Value Capital Method for calculating the tax, if I have a preference.

Then navigate to corp.delaware.gov/paytaxes/, locate our entity using the file number, and populate the annual report and franchise tax payment form fields with the information gathered above: entity details, registered agent info if requested, officer/director information for the annual report, and the calculated or entered tax amount. Do NOT enter any payment card or bank account details, and do not submit or finalize the payment.

When the form is fully populated and ready for review, capture a summary showing: the calculated franchise tax amount, any annual report fields filled in, and a screenshot or description of the completed but unsubmitted form. Present this summary to me along with the exact steps remaining to complete payment.

After preparing everything, stop for human sign-off — do not authorize, submit, or complete the payment transaction yourself, as this requires an officer's explicit approval to move company funds.

tax_001:n5.prompt:
You are helping me complete the final step of filing the Delaware franchise tax: securely archiving the confirmation receipt in {{vendor}} (cloud storage) with proper metadata so it's easy to retrieve later.

Before starting, ask me for any of these if you don't already have them:
1. The file path or location of the franchise tax confirmation receipt (PDF or screenshot) I just received.
2. My {{vendor}} account access — assume you can use your configured credentials.
3. The target folder or naming convention I want used in {{vendor}} (if I haven't specified one, propose a default like 'Compliance/DE-Franchise-Tax/{year}').
4. Any metadata fields I want captured (at minimum: company name, tax year, filing date, confirmation/receipt number, amount paid).

Actions to take:
- Upload the confirmation receipt file to {{vendor}} using its documented file-upload API (resumable/content upload as appropriate for {{vendor}}), placing it in the agreed folder with a clear filename (e.g., 'DE-Franchise-Tax-Receipt-2024.pdf').
- Set custom metadata/properties on the uploaded file via {{vendor}}'s API using the fields I provided (company name, tax year, filing date, confirmation number, amount paid).
- Verify the upload succeeded by listing or querying the file back via {{vendor}}'s API and confirming both the file content and metadata are present and correct.

Done looks like: the receipt file is stored in {{vendor}}, tagged with the specified metadata, and confirmed retrievable via an API query filtering on that metadata (e.g., tax year + document type).

Report back: the final storage path/folder, the file name, a summary of the metadata values set, and confirmation that the API-based verification query returned the correct file.
